meta.summary: Strict AI spend policy for a scaling software company with envelopes set at 2.0x sector median, governing $120k monthly across 5 teams.

shadow_ai.reimbursement_rule: AI tool purchases on personal or employee cards are not reimbursable; all AI subscriptions must be procured through the approved vendor catalog via the Finance team.

response_ladder.trigger: Team envelope reaches 75% consumption before month end
Team envelope reaches 90% consumption or single-hour burn exceeds $20
Team envelope exhausted or company envelope reaches 100%

rationales.e1: Support team production inference at $211/day runs within the $6,000 monthly Support envelope and is correctly classified as COGS under the production environment rule; no action required.
rationales.e2: Data team nightly embeddings at $38 falls well within the $25,000 Data envelope and carries no anomalous context growth; logged and passed.
rationales.e3: Search team cost per request increased 96% overnight against flat volume, breaching the 20% variance band on the Engineering envelope; Engineering lead notified to review the deploy for model routing regression or prompt bloat.
rationales.e4: Marketing team has reached 1 duplicate AI subscription this quarter, triggering the team_subscription_threshold of 1; the $30/mo ChatGPT Team charge is rerouted to the approved OpenAI enterprise contract managed by Finance.
rationales.e5: The $4,800 fine-tune request from ML Platform exceeds the $1,000 fine_tune_over_usd threshold and requires CTO approval before the job is queued; the approval checklist in the vendor catalog covers data handling and cost sign-off.
rationales.e6: The Growth team research agent hit 340 calls per hour, exceeding the 10-retry-per-task limit and the $20/hr kill threshold; the loop was terminated, preventing an estimated $1,090 in uncontrolled burn.
rationales.e7: Growth team frontier-model exception for the demo build falls within the 24-hour approval window and the $100 max_delta_usd cap; CFO approval granted and usage is time-boxed to the approved window.
rationales.e8: A junior engineer personal API key at 22x baseline with no project tag triggers ladder step 2 throttle; Engineering lead is notified to attribute the spend to a valid project tag before access is restored, preserving the experimentation carve-out once tagged.
rationales.e9: The procurement agent dataset license purchase of $499 falls within the $500 single_txn_ceiling_usd and the data-licensing merchant scope on the agent card; transaction approved and logged.
rationales.e10: The Design team AI video tool at $89/mo duplicates a Sales-held license at $1,400/yr running at 40% seat utilization; consolidating onto the existing contract recovers $840 in annualized unused seat value and the new charge is blocked.
rationales.e11: The $120 charge from an unrecognized inference provider in Engineering is flagged under the require_approval new_provider_rule; the charge is held pending CTO sign-off and completion of the security and data-terms questionnaire.
rationales.e12: Inference tagged to internal-tooling was misclassified as COGS; the internal-tooling project_tag rule reclassifies this spend to OpEx, correcting the cost-of-revenue line for the period.
rationales.e13: Month-to-date spend at 87% of the company envelope with 9 days remaining has crossed the 75% burn_alert_pct threshold; the alert was issued at 75% and the current position triggers ladder step 2 throttling on discretionary workloads.
rationales.e14: Weekly rollup complete; all team envelopes reconciled, classification rules applied, and no unresolved policy exceptions carried into the next period.
